mechanism_log: The system has a structured causal architecture with clear input-output groupings. Y3 is a linear combination of ONLY X1 and X3 (≈0.53*X1 + 0.70*X3, R²=0.87), with all other inputs having exactly zero effect. Y4 is driven primarily by X2 and X4 (both positive) and X6 (negative), with a small X1 contribution (R²=0.95). Y2 is dominated by X3 (strongly negative — high X3 reduces Y2), X6 (positive — bad), X4 (negative — good), and weakly by X1 and X2. Y1 depends on all six inputs, but X5 exhibits a sharp threshold/switch at ~X5=0.45: below it Y1 collapses toward negative values, above it Y1 plateaus at a ceiling (~0.244 at base settings). Key conflicts: X2 and X6 both increase Y1 but also raise Y2 (bad for minimization); X6 increases Y1 but decreases Y4. X3 is uniquely beneficial — it increases Y1, strongly decreases Y2, and satisfies the Y3 constraint, with no cost to Y4. The Y3 ≥ 0.4 constraint requires approximately 0.53*X1 + 0.70*X3 ≥ 0.40.

The system has a modular, nonlinear architecture. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 (linear, confirmed). Y4 depends on X2, X4 (positive) and X6 (negative) in a near-linear fashion. Y1 is driven by a strongly synergistic (multiplicative/superadditive) interaction between X2 and X4 — at high X2×X4 conditions, the marginal gradient of each nearly triples (dY1/dX2 rises from 0.38 at base to 1.28 at high-X2 high-X4). X5 acts as a hard switch for Y1: above ~0.45 it contributes fully, below that Y1 collapses rapidly toward negative. Y2 is highly nonlinear: at low X2/X4 conditions, X6 positively contributes to Y2 (base gradient +0.13), but at high X2/X4 with low X6, increasing X6 actually REDUCES Y2 (gradient −0.14). The same sign-flip occurs for X4→Y2. X3 is the most 'aligned' input — always beneficial for Y1, Y3, and Y2 simultaneously. The main Pareto frontier is swept by X2 and X6: high X2 and moderate X6 maximize Y1, but drive Y2 up; the only way to get low Y2 is to sacrifice Y1 by reducing X2. X3=1.0, X4=1.0, X5≥0.5 are essentially free wins across all objectives.

The system has a modular, strongly nonlinear architecture with confirmed interaction terms. Y3 = f(X1, X3) exclusively (R²=0.855, linear). Y4 = f(X2, X4, X6) with small X1 contribution (R²=0.947, near-linear). Y1 is a synergistic function of all inputs — the X2×X4 interaction amplifies marginal effects 2-3× at high values (dY1/dX2 rises from 0.38 at base to 1.28 at high-X2/X4; Y1=1.132 achieved vs linear prediction of ~0.87), and X5 acts as a binary switch (threshold ≈0.45, below which Y1 collapses to negative). Y2 is highly nonlinear: X6→Y2 reverses sign from +0.130 at base to −0.141 at high X2/X4 low-X6 conditions, and X4→Y2 also reverses from −0.088 to +0.250 — driven by an X2×X4 interaction term. Calibration 2 confirmed X4 limits the Y1 synergy: [0.601, 0.806, 0.698, 0.466, 0.833, 0.250] gave Y1=0.269 vs my predicted 0.40, because X4=0.466 suppresses the X2×X4 amplification. Pareto extremes identified: Y1 max=1.132 at all-max inputs [1,1,1,1,0.9,1]; Y4 max=0.321 at [0.9,1,1,1,0.8,0.1]; Y2 min=0.071 at [1,0.1,1,1,0.7,0.1]. The main Pareto tradeoff is Y4 vs (Y1, Y2): high X6 maximizes Y1 and actually reduces Y2 at high X2/X4, but strongly reduces Y4. X3=1.0, X4=1.0, X5≥0.5 are free wins across all objectives.

The system has a confirmed modular, strongly nonlinear architecture with multiplicative interactions. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 (linear, R²=0.855: Y3≈0.488·X1+0.740·X3−0.037). Y4 depends on X2 and X4 (positive) and X6 (negative) with small X1 contribution (R²=0.947, near-linear throughout all regimes). Y1 is driven by a strong X2×X4 synergistic interaction: at high X2/X4, marginal gradients amplify 2–3× (dY1/dX2 rises from 0.38 at base to 1.28 at max X2/X4), enabling Y1>1.0. X5 is a binary switch: below X5≈0.45 Y1 collapses to negative values; above it Y1 plateaus (gradient ≈4×10⁻⁵). Y2 is highly nonlinear with a documented sign reversal: X6→Y2 is +0.130 at base but −0.141 to −0.147 in the high-X2/X4 regime. This sign-flip was the critical insight enabling simultaneous high-Y1 and low-Y2. The main Pareto tradeoff is Y4 vs (Y1,Y2): X6 drives Y1 up and Y2 down (in the high-X2/X4 regime) but always drives Y4 down. X3=1.0, X4=1.0, X5≥0.5 are free wins across all objectives. Final Pareto: 17 non-dominated points, hypervolume=0.2716 (2.56× improvement from 0.106 at optimization start). Y1 max=1.132 at [1,1,1,1,0.9,1], Y4 max=0.322 at [1,1,1,1,0.9,0.1], Y2 min=0.071 at [1,0.1,1,1,0.7,0.1]. All optimized Pareto points satisfy Y3≥0.993.

iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has a confirmed modular, strongly nonlinear architecture with multiplicative interactions. Y3 depends ONLY on X1 and X3 (linear, R²=0.855: Y3≈0.488·X1+0.740·X3−0.037). Y4 depends on X2 and X4 (positive) and X6 (negative) with small X1 contribution (R²=0.947, near-linear throughout all regimes). Y1 is driven by a strong X2×X4 synergistic interaction: at high X2/X4, marginal gradients amplify 2–3× (dY1/dX2 rises from 0.38 at base to 1.28 at max X2/X4), enabling Y1>1.0. X5 is a binary switch: below X5≈0.45 Y1 collapses to negative values; above it Y1 plateaus (gradient ≈4×10⁻⁵). Y2 is highly nonlinear with a documented sign reversal: X6→Y2 is +0.130 at base but −0.141 to −0.147 in the high-X2/X4 regime. This sign-flip was the critical insight enabling simultaneous high-Y1 and low-Y2. The main Pareto tradeoff is Y4 vs (Y1,Y2): X6 drives Y1 up and Y2 down (in the high-X2/X4 regime) but always drives Y4 down. X3=1.0, X4=1.0, X5≥0.5 are free wins across all objectives. Final Pareto: 17 non-dominated points, hypervolume=0.2716 (2.56× improvement from 0.106 at optimization start). Y1 max=1.132 at [1,1,1,1,0.9,1], Y4 max=0.322 at [1,1,1,1,0.9,0.1], Y2 min=0.071 at [1,0.1,1,1,0.7,0.1]. All optimized Pareto points satisfy Y3≥0.993.

The X6 sign-flip exploitation was the decisive optimization strategy: tracing the curve [X3=1,X4=1,X5=0.8–0.9,X2=1,varying X6 from 0.1 to 1.0] revealed that Y2 decreases monotonically as X6 increases in this regime, while Y1 increases, at cost of Y4.
